\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Parse}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Input-dependent computation bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.bnd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.bnd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and a Boolean list $y$, define the
bound $B_N(y)=(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$, where $W_N$ is the machine-dependent width parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[A list length bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.bnd}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let $y$ be a
finite Boolean string. If $W$ is the machine-dependent quantity defined by the codec,
then $|y| \le (8W+8)(|y|+1)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering a bit from the encoded first component]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_fst}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_fst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairEncode_getD, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
For bit strings $u,v$ and an index $i<|u|$, the bit of their self-delimiting pairing at
position $2i$ is $u_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering a bit from the encoded second component]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_snd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_snd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairEncode_getD_snd, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For bit strings $u,v$ and any natural number $j$, the bit of their self-delimiting
pairing at position $2|u|+2+j$ equals the bit of $v$ at position $j$, with positions
beyond a string's end interpreted as false.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Dropping the encoded first component]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pe_drop}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pe_drop}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.dbl, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode_eq_dbl}
\difficulty{3}
For any bit strings $u$ and $v$, dropping the first $2|u|+2$ bits from their
self-delimiting pairing $\langle u,v\rangle$ yields exactly $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Canonicality from the default last bit]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.canon_of_getLastD}
\label{Complexity.Codec.canon_of_getLastD}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Canon, Complexity.LogProg.drop_canon}
\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ be a finite Boolean string. If its last bit, with the convention that the
default value for the empty string is true, is true, then either $w$ is empty or its
final bit is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Final bit of a binary word]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.getLastD_bits}
\label{Complexity.Codec.getLastD_bits}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.canon_bits}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $s$, the final entry of its binary bit list, using true as the
default if the list is empty, is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Value bound from bit width]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_le_of_width}
\label{Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_le_of_width}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_lt_two_pow, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ be a positive natural number, and let $w$ be a finite Boolean list whose length
is at most the length of the binary expansion of $L$. For every natural number $i$, the
binary value of the list obtained by dropping the first $i$ bits of $w$ is at most $2L$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Final bit of a canonical word]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.getLastD_of_canon}
\label{Complexity.Codec.getLastD_of_canon}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Canon, Complexity.LogProg.drop_canon}
\difficulty{1}
If a bit string $w$ has final bit true whenever it is nonempty, then its final entry,
using true as the default when it is empty, is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reaching rejection gives a rejecting halt]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.halt_rej}
\label{Complexity.Codec.halt_rej}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.orc, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.ret, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.PreS}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, let a
computation mode, input bit string $y$, register bound $B$, control label $l$, and
register valuation $v$ be given. Suppose the codec machine determined by $N$ and the
mode reaches its rejection label from configuration $(l,v)$, with all intermediate
configurations satisfying the execution guard, and suppose every register in the
resulting valuation $v'$ is at most $B$. Then the machine halts with answer false from
$(l,v)$, with every configuration before halting satisfying that same guard.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded register-program scan]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.sw_run}
\label{Complexity.Codec.sw_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.cast, Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_le_of_width, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.canon_of_getLastD, Complexity.Codec.cpDst, Complexity.Codec.cpSrc, Complexity.Codec.cp_run, Complexity.Codec.ct_run, Complexity.Codec.dcAcc, Complexity.Codec.dcBase, Complexity.Codec.dcPtr, Complexity.Codec.dcStride, Complexity.Codec.dc_run, Complexity.Codec.getLastD_of_canon, Complexity.Codec.halt_rej, Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd, Complexity.Codec.orc, Complexity.Codec.rCap, Complexity.Codec.rQ1, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.Canon, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $y$ be a Boolean word of
positive length, let $R$ be a register assignment, and let $p$ be a natural number.
Write $B=(8W+8)(|y|+1)$, where $W$ is the chunk width determined by $N$. Suppose every
register of $R$ is at most $B$, $R_L=|y|$, $R_P=p\le |y|$, and
$R_{Q1}=R_{Cap}=R_{Q2}=R_S=R_T=0$. Then either the suffix $y[p:]$ has canonical form
(every nonempty such word ends in $1$) and length at most the binary expansion length of
$|y|$, and there are $q_1,cap\le B$ such that the codec program in the chosen mode
reaches its next designated state with $Q1=q_1$, $Cap=cap$, $Q2=p$, and $S$ equal to the
binary value of $y[p:]$, while satisfying its guard; or that suffix condition fails and
the program halts with answer false while satisfying its guard throughout.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[First encoded shape predicate]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Shape1}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Shape1}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
For Boolean lists $y,x,w$ and a natural number $s$, the first shape condition holds
exactly when $y$ is the pair encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of $w$ with the
binary digit list of $s$, and the length of that digit list is at most the length of the
binary digit list of $|y|$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Second encoded shape predicate]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Shape2}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Shape2}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
For Boolean lists $y,x,w,w'$ and a natural number $s$, the second shape condition holds
exactly when $y$ is the pair encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of $w$ with the pair
encoding of $w'$ and the binary digit list of $s$, and the length of that digit list is
at most the length of the binary digit list of $|y|$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Parsing a paired input]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.parse_x}
\label{Complexity.Codec.parse_x}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.cast, Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le, Complexity.Codec.Regs.upd_P, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val_P, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.cpDst, Complexity.Codec.cpSrc, Complexity.Codec.cp_run, Complexity.Codec.halt_rej, Complexity.Codec.len_run, Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd, Complexity.Codec.orc, Complexity.Codec.pr_run, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let
$\mathrm{mode}$ be one of valid, initial, accepting, or step mode, and let $y$ be a
finite bit string. Either $y=\langle x,r\rangle$ for some bit strings $x,r$, and the
program in mode $\mathrm{mode}$ reaches its first parsing-test stage from its initial
length scan, with all registers bounded by $(8W+8)(|y|+1)$ at every earlier step, where
$W$ is the machine-dependent width defined for $N$; or $y$ has no such pair
representation and the program halts with answer false from its initial length scan,
with all registers bounded by that same bound at every earlier step.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parsing run of the codec program]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.parse_run}
\label{Complexity.Codec.parse_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.cast, Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le, Complexity.Codec.Regs.upd_P, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val_P, Complexity.Codec.Shape1, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.halt_rej, Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd, Complexity.Codec.orc, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.parse_x, Complexity.Codec.pe_drop, Complexity.Codec.prCont, Complexity.Codec.pr_run, Complexity.Codec.sw_run, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.LogProg.canon_bits, Complexity.LogProg.canon_eq_bits, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let
$\mathrm{mode}$ be any codec mode other than the step mode. For every bit string $y$,
either there exist bit strings $x,w$ and natural numbers $s,q_1,c$ such that $y=\langle
x,\langle w,\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$, $|\mathrm{bits}(s)|\leq
|\mathrm{bits}(|y|)|$, $q_1,c\leq (8W+8)(|y|+1)$, and the codec register program,
started at its length-scan label with all registers zero and run with its two membership
oracles on input $y$, reaches the label for halving the auxiliary counter. At that point
its registers satisfy $L=|y|$, $P=2|x|+2|w|+4$, $A=2|x|+2$, $Q_1=q_1$, $Cap=c$,
$Q_2=2|x|+2|w|+4$, and $S=s$; or no such encoded representation of $y$ exists, and the
program, from the same initial configuration, halts with answer false. In both cases,
the execution respects its configuration precondition and every register is bounded by
$(8W+8)(|y|+1)$ throughout.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parsing a triple-encoded input]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.parse_run₂}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.cast, Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le, Complexity.Codec.Regs.upd_P, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val_P, Complexity.Codec.Shape2, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.cpDst, Complexity.Codec.cpSrc, Complexity.Codec.cp_run, Complexity.Codec.halt_rej, Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd, Complexity.Codec.orc, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.parse_x, Complexity.Codec.pe_drop, Complexity.Codec.prCont, Complexity.Codec.pr_run, Complexity.Codec.sw_run, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.LogProg.canon_bits, Complexity.LogProg.canon_eq_bits, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let $y$ be a
finite bit string. Either there are bit strings $x,w,w'$ and natural numbers
$s,q_1,\mathrm{cap}$ such that $y=\langle x,\langle w,\langle
w',\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$, the binary expansion of $s$ has length at
most the length of the binary expansion of $|y|$, and $q_1,\mathrm{cap}\le
(8W+8)(|y|+1)$, where $W$ is the machine-dependent width defined for $N$. In this case
the step-mode program reaches its $N_1$ copy stage from its initial length scan, with
all registers bounded by $(8W+8)(|y|+1)$ at every earlier step, and with register values
$L=|y|$, $P=2|x|+2|w|+2|w'|+6$, $A=2|x|+2$, $B=2|x|+2|w|+4$, $Q_1=q_1$,
$\mathrm{Cap}=\mathrm{cap}$, $Q_2=2|x|+2|w|+2|w'|+6$, and $S=s$ at that stage.
Otherwise, if no such triple and $s$ satisfy the encoding and binary-length condition,
the program halts with answer false from its initial length scan, with all registers
bounded by the same bound at every earlier step.
\end{theorem}
